cards.term: Example of interchangeable parts: Jerome's one-day clock
cards.def: After the Panic of 1837 almost ruined him, Chauncey Jerome made a cheap brass "one-day" clock with interchangeable parts in one New Haven factory, because wooden-works clocks could not be exported when humidity swelled the wood.

cards.term: Example of a market without timely news: Burrows's potatoes
cards.def: In 1844 John Burrows shipped 2,500 bushels of potatoes from Davenport toward a $2 New Orleans price, but after six weeks on a flatboat the market was glutted and he swapped them at 8 cents a bushel for coffee.

cards.term: Example of the cotton gin's effect
cards.def: Before the gin, a laborer cleaned about 1 pound of sticky short-fiber cotton a day; with Whitney's machine one laborer cleaned 50 pounds, and by 1840 cotton was almost two-thirds of all U.S. exports.

cards.term: Example of the Erie Canal's payoff
cards.def: The 364-mile state-built canal from Albany to Buffalo paid for itself in a few years, cut the Buffalo-to-New York freight cost from more than 19 cents a mile to less than 3, and made towns like Rochester and Lockport boom.

cards.term: Example of steamboat speed on western rivers
cards.def: The upstream trip from New Orleans to Louisville fell from 90 days to 8, costs dropped 90 percent, and steamboats, following Fulton's 1807 Clermont, became the key to manufacturing in the Ohio and upper Mississippi valleys.

cards.term: Example of a Marshall Court contract case: Fletcher v. Peck
cards.def: Georgia tried to revoke a land grant obtained by bribing legislators, but the Court unanimously held that the grant was a contract and that states may not impair "the obligation of contracts."

cards.term: Example of interstate commerce: Gibbons v. Ogden
cards.def: The Court struck down New York's steamboat monopoly, defined commerce broadly, and said Congress's power could be "exercised to its utmost extent," which opened the way to more business competition.

cards.term: Example of the Lowell mills as a model factory town
cards.def: The Boston Associates employed daughters of New England farm families, housed them in company boardinghouses with a 10 p.m. curfew, offered lectures and a library, and paid $2.40 to $3.20 a week for 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., six days a week.

cards.term: Example of factories remaking the waterscape: Lowell and Lawrence
cards.def: By 1836 seven canals served 26 Lowell mills, and at Lawrence a dam 32 feet high and 1,600 feet across, then the world's largest, helped control New Hampshire lakes, while waste in the river spread typhoid, cholera, and dysentery.

cards.term: Example of a craft becoming assembly-line work: Lynn shoes
cards.def: Micajah Pratt hired up to 500 workers, standardized patterns, and used sole-cutting machines, while women sewed uppers and men attached bottoms, so shoemaking ceased to be a start-to-finish craft within a generation.

cards.term: Example of a worker's protest: Sam Patch
cards.def: In 1827 Sam Patch leapt 70 feet at Passaic Falls to protest a mill owner's private "Forest Gardens" park, later jumped at Niagara, and drowned at Genesee Falls, calling the leap "an art which I have knowledge of and courage to perform."

cards.term: Example of a town transformed by a canal: Kingston, New York
cards.def: Kingston had about 1,000 people in 1820, but after the 1828 Delaware and Hudson Canal linked it to Pennsylvania coalfields it gained banks, specialized stores, and gas lamps, and by 1850 its population was 10,000.

cards.term: Example of a western settlement entering the market: Sugar Creek, Illinois
cards.def: First settled in 1817, Sugar Creek was still partly a barter world, but Eddin Lewis also drove hogs to St. Louis for cash and in 1848 shipped 6,000 pounds of barreled pork and lard and 350 bushels of corn.

cards.term: Example of the Panic of 1819's trigger
cards.def: Liverpool bid cotton up to 32.5 cents a pound in 1818, then the price collapsed, land values fell 50 to 75 percent almost overnight, and new southwestern cotton planters, tightly tied to the world market, were hit especially hard.
